question: Is VoxCPM2 better than MMS on Khmer-English mixed sentences, and does CER see it?
setup: bench/pilot_v1 mixed, 25 sentences x 2 systems, 1 native rater, blind, loudness-normalized, ITU-T P.800 1-5
verdict: VoxCPM2 far better; plain CER is not valid for mixed sentences

question: Does UTMOSv2 track native Khmer ratings?
setup: 30 rated mixed clips, UTMOSv2 fold 0, 5 crops
verdict: No; dropped as a quality metric

question: Does writing English words in Khmer script help sengtha?
verdict: Helps (+0.8 MOS) but the voice itself is the larger gap -> distillation

question: How good is Gemini 3.8 TTS on KhmerTTS-Bench v1?
setup: 320 sentences, raw text, voice Callirrhoe, no style prefix
verdict: Most accurate system; Samleng competes on small/offline/open/native sound

question: Does CER with English in Khmer script on both sides track human ratings?
setup: mixed_v2 (50 clips) and translit_v0 (75 clips) owner MOS, per-sentence Spearman, bootstrap CI
verdict: Adopted mixed CER for mixed sentences; it measures correctness, not naturalness

question: Does fine-tuning sengtha (VITS, ~36M at inference) on VoxCPM2 audio in its own cloned voice improve Khmer and unseen English words?
setup: distill v1: 1.21 h (465 mixed + 931 OpenSLR-text clips), English in Latin script, batch 16, lr 1e-4, MPS; bench v1 300 Khmer sentences, verbalized, mixed CER vs base
verdict: Works: about 43% fewer all-Khmer errors at step 16000, and never-seen English words improve too. Side effects: the student drifts toward the teacher's faster pace (0.86x duration at 16k) and numbers wobble late in training (5.8% at 14k, 2.5% at 16k) because the v1 text has no number sentences.
next: Pick the final checkpoint by ear (14k vs 16k vs an average, length_scale adjusted); variant B; big run on ~9 h (v1+v2 numbers/mixed+v3 Wikipedia).

question: Does re-generating rejected teacher clips with another seed rescue them?
verdict: Yes; queued for v2 (seeds 1, 2) and v3

question: Which voice should Samleng speak in? Owner: sengtha sounds a bit old; wants a ~20-year-old female teacher.
setup: VoxCPM2 voice design: 4 English descriptions x 3 seeds on one teacher sentence; owner picked one clip; 12-sentence clone test (mixed, numbers, long wiki, KHQR) with it as reference.
result: Owner picked 'clear' take 1 (confident young woman, clear crisp youthful, friendly teacher tone) and confirmed the clone test stays the same voice. v1-A step 17000 (owner's pick by ear): ALL 10.4 -> 6.7, better on 183/300, speed 0.90 (no flag) vs step 16000 5.9 but speed 0.86.
verdict: New teacher voice = outputs/voice/teacher_clear.wav (synthetic, no consent issue). Re-record v1+v2+v3 (6,835 sentences) as batches v1c/v2c/v3c; old-voice v3 jobs skipped.
next: Variant B finishes first (A vs B on sengtha data), then the big run on v1c+v2c+v3c with the winner.

question: English in Latin script (A) or Khmer script (B) for the student's input?
setup: Same v1 audio (1.2 h, sengtha voice). A step 17000 fed Latin; B step 6000 fed approved Khmer spellings; base sengtha fed the same Khmer spellings (eval_checkpoint --translit); bench v1 mixed split, mixed CER, paired Wilcoxon
verdict: Khmer script wins for words that have an approved spelling: B reaches the teacher's level on mixed sentences, and spelling alone (no training) already beats trained A. Unknown words have no approved spelling at run time, so the big run trains on both scripts; dictionary words go through Khmer script by default.
next: Big run with both spellings of every English sentence.

question: How much do bench scores move by chance, and do an averaged checkpoint or steadier playback help?
setup: A step 17000 on bench v1 (300 sentences): seeds 0/1/2; average of checkpoints 15000+16000+17000; duration noise 0.6 -> 0.3 -> 0; voice noise 0.5 -> 0.3. Teacher VoxCPM2 (clear voice, spoken-form text, hints) on the same sentences.
verdict: Noise floor is about 1 point on the all-Khmer median and about 3 points per category: single-seed gaps below that are not real. Averaging checkpoints gives no measurable gain. Lower duration noise is a real, small gain (about 1 point; beats all three default seeds). The teacher scores 3.1, so the student (5.7-6.8) still has 3 points of headroom.
next: Owner rates default vs steady timing blind (study student_v1); if it does not sound flat, duration noise 0 or 0.3 becomes the default. Score finals with 3 seeds.

question: How natural does the trained student sound next to base, its teacher and Gemini 3.8?
setup: Blind 1-5 MOS, 1 rater (the owner), 25 bench sentences (8 pure, 5 names, 5 numbers, 7 mixed) x 5 systems: base sengtha, student = run A step 17000 (Latin input), student_steady = same with duration noise 0, teacher = VoxCPM2 in sengtha's voice, Gemini 3.8. Per-sentence paired Wilcoxon.
verdict: Training raised naturalness by more than a point over base (2.16 -> 3.40). Steady timing is better by ear as well as by CER: new default. The student is 0.3 below its teacher (inside the 0.7 gate), and the teacher equals Gemini 3.8. The gap is almost all in mixed sentences (3.0 vs 3.86), where this student read English in Latin letters. One rater, 25 sentences.
next: Rate run B (Khmer-script English) on the mixed sentences in the next round; big run; multi-rater study. No case yet for a new model type (Phase E).

question: Which checkpoint of the big clear-voice run (060) is best, and does slowing the student at playback (length scale) cost accuracy?
setup: distill_v2_clear, bench v1 (300 Khmer sentences), steady timing, 3 seeds. Pick: steps 10000 vs 16000 at length scale 1.81, Latin and Khmer-script input. Pace: step 10000 at length scales 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.65 (Latin).
verdict: The two checkpoints are equal. Playback slowing does not cost: native pace is 3 points worse than 1.65, and 1.3 vs 1.65 is a tie. The gap to run A (5.7) is not the stretch.
next: C7e data-mix test (job 062: v1c+v4c+v5c only, to step 8000); skip C7c/C7d.

question: Why does the big clear-voice run (060) stop at ~8.5-9 when run A reached 5.7: missing data, or a model that cannot fit its data?
setup: 060 step 10000 (also 4000, 18000), steady timing, length scale 1.81: 180 sentences it trained on (stratified by source) + 89 held-out clips of the same run; teacher's own clips and base on the same text; mixed CER, same judge. One seed. Script outputs/train/eval/seen_test.py on the Mac mini.
verdict: Underfitting, not missing data: the model reads its own training sentences no better than unseen ones and about twice as badly as its teacher; no gain after step 10000. More data of the same kind or more passes will not fix it. Leading suspect: the training audio is too fast for this model (2.7 audio frames per input token vs 4.5 in the base model's own speech; the student copies the teacher's speed exactly). The C7b pace test only measured playback slowing, not training on fast audio, so its 'skip C7c/d' rule was wrong.
next: C7c/C7d after all: slow the teacher audio (rubberband R3, pitch kept), owner listens (outputs/voice/slow_test/listen.html: original / x1.25 / x1.45), then a 6000-step test run on slowed audio vs 060 step 6000.
